argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean, caveat-free certification. It does support a narrower position: certification is defensible only as caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure of the unresolved developer-support migration limitation and the fact that the mitigation artifact remains draft. Aggregate readiness passing by 2.5 points and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are relevant support for overall launch readiness, but they do not negate the specific below-target migration slice or convert an unapproved draft runbook into completed mitigation. The overbroad part of the original framing is any implication that current monitoring guidance alone cures the policy gap. The supportable reading is that the same evidence justifies allowing certification to proceed only with the limitation clearly carried into the certification packet rather than treating the record as clean compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim of business necessity is required to support that narrower position. The practical consequence is simply that treating this as caveated rather than suspicious preserves a path to certification while aligning the packet to the actual record.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy in the record is narrow: certification without material caveats requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. That standard is not met here. But the policy text does not forbid certification with a material caveat; it requires disclosure of material limitations unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the present record, the compliant interpretation is therefore not clean certification, but certification only in a caveated form that expressly discloses the unresolved limitation and draft mitigation status.
concessions: The current evidence does not establish clean compliance.
The draft runbook cannot be counted as approved mitigation because required approval and threshold fields are still missing.
The current model-card draft is inconsistent with the proposed disclosure position because it says there are no known material limitations.
There is no formal materiality determination in the record for the developer-support migration issue.
